text: Dretske's relevant-alternatives theory holds that knowing that P requires ruling out only the ___ alternatives, so that the brain-in-a-vat hypothesis—not being one of them in ordinary contexts—need not be eliminated.
explanation: On Dretske's view, knowledge requires eliminating only the alternatives that are relevant in the context, not every logically possible one; since the BIV scenario is not a relevant alternative in ordinary contexts, failing to rule it out does not defeat ordinary knowledge. This blocks the skeptical argument by restricting closure to relevant alternatives.
